content:
Former Apple design chief Jony Ive has long described his vision for the iPhone's design as "a single sheet of glass." It's widely believed that even years after Ive's departure, Apple still upholds this goal, and Liquid Glass represents the software design that paves the way for Apple's next generation of hardware.

We've learned from multiple reports that the 20th anniversary edition iPhone may bring us closer to Apple's vision in several ways, and the latest news could be another piece of the puzzle...

What to expect

There were earlier speculations that Apple might launch a standalone 20th anniversary special edition iPhone, but more recent reports indicate that all the features designed to achieve the "all-glass" design will ultimately land on the iPhone 19 Pro. To complicate matters further, some believe that to highlight the anniversary significance, Apple will skip the iPhone 19 naming and go straight to iPhone 20 Pro.

With the launch still far off, the reports remain highly speculative, but the most anticipated design highlight is expected to be a display that curves toward the edges on all four sides, creating the illusion of a bezel-less screen.

It's almost certain that this will be the year Apple finally succeeds in embedding the Face ID module under the screen, and the market also hopes the front camera and speaker can be hidden beneath the display as well.

Combined, these elements will deliver a highly convincing "single sheet of glass" appearance.

Glass back

Leaker Fixed Focus Digital recently revealed another element of the overall design: the back will return to a glass material, replacing the aluminum used in recent models.

While a glass back will make the device more fragile, it undoubtedly helps realize the "single sheet of glass" design philosophy. Would you consider this an acceptable trade-off in pursuit of a futuristic design? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
